Test UREA Method Observed Value Units Biological Reference Range Sample
UREA Urease,dye 26 mg/dL 10 - 45 SERUM

NOTE: A high serum urea level occurs in acute and chronic renal failure, pyelonephritis, urinary tract obstruction and shock. High levels are also seen in severe congestive heart failure, hyperalimentation, diabetic ketoacidosis, tissue damage associated with trauma, dehydration and bleeding from the gastrointestinal tract.

Low levels occurs in pregnancy, with decreased protein intake, acute liver failure and with intravenous fluid administration.

CREATININE Enzymatic 0.9 mg/dL Newborn (1-7 days) : 0.6 - 1.1 Infant (8-31 days) : 0.3 - 0.7 Children (31 days-1yr) : 0.4 - 0.7 Adult: Children (1 yr - 14 yrs) : 0.2 - 0.7 Male : 0.7 - 1.5 Female : 0.6 - 1.5 SERUM

Technology used: Samples tested on VITROS - Drychemistry Analyzers with intellicheck technology

NOTE: Several factors may influence serum creatinine independent of changes in GFR. Decreased levels are seen in individuals with small stature, elderly persons with decreased muscle mass, cachexia, amputation or muscle diseases and pregnancy.

Because some renal clearance of creatinine is due to tubular secretion, drugs that inhibit this secretory component (eg, cimetidine and trimethoprim) may cause small increases in serum creatinine without an actual decrease in GFR. Patients on long term lidocaine therapy may show an increase in serum creatinine levels.

C-REACTIVE PROTEIN (CRP)* Nephelometry 5.0 mg/L < 10 SERUM

Technology used: Samples tested on VITROS - Drychemistry Analyzers with intellcheck technology

Comments
1. CRP is an acute phase reactant which is used in inflammatory disorders for monitoring course and effect of therapy. It is most useful as an indicator of activity in Rheumatoid arthritis, Rheumatic fever, tissue injury or necrosis and infections.
2. As compared to ESR, CRP shows an earlier rise in inflammatory disorders which begins in 4-6 hrs, the intensity of the rise being higher than ESR and the recovery being earlier than ESR.
3. Unlike ESR, CRP levels are not influenced by hematologic conditions like Anemia, Polycythemia etc
